title: Require a complete post-cutover schema authorship ledger
decision_statement: Before instance-layer self-hosting is implemented, enumerate every schema in the post-RFC-038 contract and assign each an authoritative source Type or Types, extension dependencies, emitter, and generated status or explicit exclusion rationale.

sources.excerpt: The owner requires a ledger for all 24 then-known schema files before authoring, including extension and envelope schemas and explicit emitter-owned outputs.
The current task scope updates the ledger for the complete post-RFC-038 schema set and explicitly calls out manifest, Relation, and relations-collection dispositions.

alternatives: Begin with the named instance entities and discover unclassified schemas during implementation.
Carry the pre-RFC schema count forward as the target.
accepted_cost: Implementation waits for a larger, evolving inventory, including schemas whose ownership is not yet assigned.
supersedes: The six-entity instance-layer scope implied by the earlier #272 description

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A convenient partial inventory could silently omit effective contracts and make the authorship claim false.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The ledger may give explicit exclusion rationales instead of forcing every artifact into the semantic model.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Inventory work expands without assigning actionable ownership or reaching implementation.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: A source flip scoped only to the obvious files could strand existing schema consumers and corpus trees.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The ledger is explicitly recounted after architectural changes rather than freezing the old file set.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Historic artifacts are retained merely because they appeared in the old count.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different schema classes could acquire unrelated or unrecorded authorship rules.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Emitter-owned and genuinely excluded artifacts remain legitimate when their boundary is explicit and tested.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Completeness is interpreted as requiring one mechanism for artifacts with materially different roles.

coding_notes: Counts the explicit owner-imposed coverage gate, not any unresolved content disposition inside a ledger row. Later coordinator prose about additional files is supporting scope evidence only.

title: Model each surviving instance shape once
decision_statement: Instance-layer self-hosting models each surviving semantic shape once and obtains extension-owned facets through effective inherited Types rather than duplicating the shape for every schema copy or flattening extension fields into core.

sources.excerpt: The current scope says to model each surviving RFC-031 shape once, model SourceReference once, and use effective inherited Types for extension-owned facets such as Relation federation IDs.
The effective schema demonstrates one embedded Relation shape carrying extension-owned federation properties, the concrete duplication this rule must replace.

alternatives: Model every copied schema occurrence independently.
Flatten all extension-contributed fields into the core instance Type.
accepted_cost: Emitters and resolvers must understand inheritance and reuse a source shape across multiple output locations.
supersedes: RFC-031's file-to-prose mapping as the target self-hosting model
derived_from: RFC-031's 18 rows representing only 15 semantic shapes

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Copied or flattened definitions could drift or misstate which package owns a semantic facet.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: One source shape may still emit into every concrete schema location consumers need.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Semantic factoring makes generated artifacts hard for ordinary consumers to locate or understand.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the old one-row-per-copy structure would carry known duplication into the self-hosted model.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Every surviving output location remains accounted for in the ledger.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Deduplication removes a compatibility surface without a generated replacement.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Independent copies could disagree about the same SourceReference or Relation semantics.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Extension packages retain ownership of their facets through inheritance rather than core absorption.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared coherence collapses legitimate extension ownership into the core package.

coding_notes: This is the instance-layer application of F1's inheritance precedent. Individual content choices below remain separate and unresolved.

title: Settle whether tags belong to the affected instance shapes
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided, entity by entity, whether schema-only or published-copy-only tags on Record, TypedRecord, Note, NoteSection, Container, and Vocabulary belong in their self-hosted semantic Types or should be removed from the conflicting artifact.

sources.excerpt: Record.tags is schema-only and the issue requires an explicit add-to-prose or remove-from-schema decision.
TypedRecord.tags has the same unresolved schema-versus-prose disposition.
Note and NoteSection tags expose a published-record versus shadow-record disagreement whose semantic content remains for #272.
The effective Note schema currently defines free-form tags as non-semantic discovery labels.

alternatives: Model tags consistently on all affected instance Types.
Remove tags from schemas or published prose where no semantic contract is intended.
Choose different dispositions per entity with explicit reasons.
accepted_cost: No cost has been accepted; the current artifacts disagree and the feeder issues remain open.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Keeping tags favors practical discovery; removing or formally typing them may better protect semantic clarity.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A convenient tag surface is mistaken for a settled semantic contract.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Either removal or formalization can change accepted instance data.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: No migration rule exists until dispositions are chosen.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A content decision is smuggled through as drift repair.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A common tags contract favors coherence while entity-specific dispositions may preserve local fit.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: No common or local policy has been chosen.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Superficially similar fields are forced into one policy without examining their meaning.

coding_notes: One unresolved cross-entity policy question. Audit should split it if #272 records distinct, independently reasoned dispositions. It is excluded from bias counts.

title: Resolve the legacy SourceReference relationType alias
decision_statement: The project has not decided whether SourceReference.relationType remains a declared compatibility alias of sourceRole or is deleted from the schema as a superseded legacy field.

sources.excerpt: The issue identifies relationType as schema-declared but prose-described only as a deprecated never-written alias and requires delete-versus-declare resolution.
The current schema still recognizes relationType while forbidding it together with sourceRole.

alternatives: Delete relationType and require sourceRole.
Declare relationType as a supported deprecated compatibility alias.
accepted_cost: No compatibility-versus-simplification cost has yet been accepted.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Alias retention aids old data but preserves two names for one role.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Legacy syntax becomes accidental current semantics.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retention protects continuity; deletion completes the RFC-023 evolution.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: No migration or deprecation window is chosen.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Compatibility is claimed without evidence of live writers or readers.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: One field name improves shared coherence; an alias tolerates locally old producers.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Two encodings survive indefinitely without an explicit compatibility contract.

coding_notes: The current schema is effective evidence but the issue explicitly disputes whether that state is intentional. Therefore this is not coded as an implemented preference.

title: Carry the attaches source role into generated SourceReference
decision_statement: SourceReference.sourceRole includes attaches; instance self-hosting must carry that already accepted value into its single source Type and generated references.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-017 requires attaches in SourceReference.sourceRole across all four schema copies and rejects modelling attachments as Relation edges.
The effective SourceReference schema includes attaches in the sourceRole enum.
The drift audit attributes attaches to RFC-017 and identifies only its omission from prose.

alternatives: Drop attaches during self-hosting despite its accepted schema meaning.
accepted_cost: The SourceReference vocabulary remains broader than the stale pseudo-IDL currently documents.
supersedes: The stale four-value SourceReference.sourceRole prose enum

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Generation from stale prose would erase an accepted semantic role.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The value remains a simple readable enum member.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Schema presence is treated as intent even when no ratified source can be found.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: This card merely carries an accepted value across representations.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: No new compatibility policy is introduced.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A mechanical reconciliation is given a separate constitutional vote.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Schema and generated reference could expose different role vocabularies.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Extensions may still define separate source-reference behavior through their own contracts.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A shared enum is expanded without an accepted semantic source.

coding_notes: Documented but excluded from bias counts because carrying an accepted RFC-017 enum member is mechanical derivation.

title: Keep Relation federation identifiers extension-owned
decision_statement: Model sourceRepositoryId and targetRepositoryId as effective inherited Relation facets owned by ext:federation rather than as fields of the core Relation Type or as unmodelled schema exceptions.

sources.excerpt: The instance-layer scope explicitly directs effective inherited Types for extension-owned facets such as Relation federation IDs.
The current schema describes sourceRepositoryId and targetRepositoryId as ext:federation-only properties.
The feeder issue records the prior ambiguity between adding federation IDs to core prose and removing them from the schema.

alternatives: Add federation repository identifiers directly to the core Relation Type.
Remove them from generated schemas.
Leave them as a hand-maintained schema exception.
accepted_cost: Consumers must resolve an effective inherited Type to see the complete Relation shape.
supersedes: Treating federation identifiers as an unexplained core-schema/prose drift

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Flattening the fields into core would obscure their semantic owner; omitting them would erase federation meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Generated effective schemas still present a directly usable complete Relation shape.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Provenance factoring makes the effective contract invisible to ordinary tooling.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the accidental flattened schema/prose split would retain known drift.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The existing on-wire field names and effective schema behavior are retained.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Architectural cleanup changes stored federation data unnecessarily.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Core ownership would collapse a bounded extension concern into the shared base model.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Inheritance produces one coherent effective Relation contract for consumers.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Extension autonomy produces incompatible effective Relation shapes or ambiguous resolution.

coding_notes: A deliberate counter-pole candidate on Coherence/Autonomy; exception classification remains none until epic bias is established.

title: Resolve Container description and identity metadata
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided whether Container.description, Container.identityInstanceId, and Container.tags are intended instance semantics to model or schema-only additions to remove.

sources.excerpt: The issue records three RFCs' worth of schema-only Container properties and requires add-to-prose or remove-from-schema dispositions.
The effective schema currently defines description, identityInstanceId, and tags with substantive constraints and provenance.

alternatives: Model all three properties in the Container Type.
Remove one or more properties from the schema after individual review.
accepted_cost: No semantic-surface or compatibility cost has been accepted.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: The properties carry useful identity and description, but their absence from prose makes intent uncertain.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Schema detail is automatically promoted to semantic intent.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Removal may break existing containers; modelling may preserve accidental additions.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: No corpus evidence or migration rule is recorded here.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Compatibility assumptions replace an explicit content decision.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: The evidence does not expose a clear coherence/autonomy tension.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: An axis is forced onto a content disposition without evidence.

coding_notes: Grouped because the issue presents these as one additive Container drift cluster; audit should split any property receiving a distinct rationale.

title: Resolve UUID enforcement for Container identifiers
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided whether Container.containerId and root/member instance IDs must be schema-enforced UUIDs or remain unconstrained strings despite their prose types.

sources.excerpt: The issue identifies missing UUID formats as an enforcement gap and requires format constraints or a reason to omit them.
The current schema describes UUID semantics while validating these identifiers only as strings.

alternatives: Add format uuid to all Container identity fields.
Deliberately allow non-UUID string identifiers and correct the prose type.
accepted_cost: No strictness-versus-data-acceptance cost has been chosen.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: UUID enforcement protects declared identity semantics but could reject practical existing strings.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A format annotation is treated as harmless when it changes validity.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Tightening validation may invalidate existing data; retaining strings perpetuates drift.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Evolution proceeds without measuring compatibility impact.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A shared UUID rule constrains local identifier choice.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: No extension or compatibility path is selected.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Local flexibility erodes cross-repository identity assumptions.

coding_notes: Separate from whether the Container fields exist because validation strictness is independently reversible.

title: Resolve lineage and provenance on Vocabulary and Term
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided whether Vocabulary and Term carry Lineage and Provenance as their published pseudo-IDL declares or omit them as their closed schemas currently require.

sources.excerpt: Vocabulary lineage and provenance are present in prose but rejected by the closed schema.
Term has the same unresolved lineage and provenance drift.
The published subsection declares lineage and provenance on both Vocabulary and Term.

alternatives: Add Lineage and Provenance to both generated schemas and source Types.
Remove the properties from published prose.
Choose different dispositions for Vocabulary and Term with explicit rationale.
accepted_cost: No provenance-richness versus schema-surface cost has been chosen.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Provenance fields protect semantic history but add model surface and authoring burden.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Provenance is retained ceremonially without reliable population or semantics.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Removal simplifies the model but may discard established lineage claims.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Current drift is mistaken for a deliberate continuity choice.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: The record does not clearly expose this axis.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: An irrelevant axis is forced into the cube.

coding_notes: The shared substrate makes this a candidate common policy; split if owner decisions diverge by entity.

title: Resolve Term createdAt requiredness
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided whether Term.createdAt is required, as the published substrate declares, or optional, as the effective schema permits.

sources.excerpt: The issue identifies the Term.createdAt optionality flip and requires a decision.
createdAt is defined but omitted from the effective schema's required list.

alternatives: Require createdAt and migrate terms missing it.
Make createdAt optional in the source Type and published structural reference.
accepted_cost: No historical-accountability versus permissive-authorship cost has been chosen.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Required creation time improves provenance but makes incomplete term authoring invalid.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: No defaulting or migration rule exists.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A timestamp is required without demonstrating semantic use.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Tightening requiredness could reject existing terms.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A validation change lands without measuring affected records.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: No shared-versus-local ownership choice is evidenced.

coding_notes: Independently reversible from lineage/provenance and therefore split.

title: Resolve RelationTypeDefinition aliases
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided whether RelationTypeDefinition supports aliases as the shared VocabularyEntry prose declares or omits them as its schema currently does.

sources.excerpt: RelationTypeDefinition.aliases is present in pseudo-IDL and absent from the schema; the issue requires a disposition.
The published substrate and RelationTypeDefinition pseudo-IDL declare aliases.

alternatives: Add aliases to RelationTypeDefinition.
Remove aliases from the specialization while retaining or revising the substrate rule.
accepted_cost: No resolution-flexibility versus vocabulary-simplicity cost has been accepted.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Aliases preserve identity through naming changes but create multiple accepted expressions.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: No collision or deprecation rule is chosen for this specialization.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Aliases can preserve old keys while vocabulary evolves; omission requires rewrites or rejection.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A single key favors shared coherence while aliases tolerate varied producers.

coding_notes: Split from the independent open-versus-closed schema choice.

title: Resolve RelationTypeDefinition's top-level extension policy
decision_statement: The project has not yet decided whether RelationTypeDefinition rejects unknown top-level fields and confines extension metadata to properties, as its prose claims, or deliberately remains open-world as its schema currently permits.

sources.excerpt: The issue identifies relation-type.json as the only audited sibling lacking additionalProperties false despite its own text claiming unknown top-level fields are rejected.
The schema provides an open properties bag whose description says unknown top-level fields are rejected, while the root lacks that rejecting keyword.

alternatives: Set additionalProperties false and require extension data in properties.
Keep top-level openness and revise the stated policy.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Closed-world validation protects the shared meaning; open-world data is easier to extend ad hoc.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The properties bag is the proposed counter-pole safeguard but has not been ratified for this fix.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Strictness rejects legitimate evolution without an extension channel, or openness admits silent semantic drift.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Closing the schema may reject existing unknown fields; leaving it open preserves an inconsistency.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A breaking validation change is called mechanical.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Closed top-level vocabulary favors coherence; open top-level fields favor local autonomy.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: A namespaced properties bag could retain autonomy if chosen.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Local extension becomes indistinguishable from shared contract evolution.

coding_notes: A direct foundational-axis tension, but no direction is coded because the effective schema and published claim conflict.

title: Flip generated artifacts to final authorship
decision_statement: After instance and definition closure, make resolved-record emitters authoritative for generated schemas and structural references, forbid hand edits to generated targets, and enforce clean-checkout regenerate-and-diff with no remainder overlay.

sources.excerpt: The open final-cutover task specifies generated-output authorship, no hand edits, no remainder overlay, and clean regenerate-and-diff acceptance.
The owner keeps #271 as the last implementation item and requires pure regenerate-and-diff, synchronized mirrors, and byte-level equality.

alternatives: Keep hand-authored schemas as authority and use generation only as an advisory comparison.
Merge a hand-maintained remainder overlay into generated output.
accepted_cost: If implemented, contributors lose direct authorship of generated structural artifacts and must change semantic source records or emitters instead.
supersedes: Hand-authored schema/reference authority for generated targets

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Directly editable projections could diverge from their semantic sources.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Generated property tables and structural references remain contributor-readable outputs.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Semantic-source discipline makes small documentation corrections prohibitively indirect.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining hand-authored authority would preserve the duplication the epic intends to replace.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The cutover is last, byte-compared, mirror-synchronized, and gated from a clean checkout.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Authorship flips before closure and parity evidence are complete.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Independent editors and consumers could maintain conflicting structural authorities.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Human narrative remains separately authored, and emitter implementations may vary when output parity holds.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One generation pipeline becomes an opaque bottleneck for all contributors.

coding_notes: Kept off historical-bias counts because the final source flip is still open and unimplemented, despite explicit owner scope.

title: Set the residual prose-schema conformance mechanism
decision_statement: For any target not covered by generated prose, the project must still choose through #274 whether and how a hardened fail-closed AST and symbol-resolving comparator replaces or retains RFC-031 coverage; generation alone does not close that residual seam.

sources.excerpt: Final acceptance is conditional on either generated prose safely replacing RFC-031 or a residual checker retained and hardened exactly as #274 decides.
The owner records that regenerate-and-diff covers records to schema but does not by itself cover prose to schema, so RFC-031 cannot simply be retired.

alternatives: Generate all structural prose and remove RFC-031 mappings for generated targets.
Retain a hardened residual comparator for genuinely ungenerated targets.
Retire RFC-031 without replacement.
accepted_cost: The exact residual mechanism and its maintenance cost remain undecided pending #274.
supersedes: The original proposal to retire RFC-031 wholesale

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Removing the only remaining signal could permit prose and schema to disagree; retaining it adds complexity where generation may suffice.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Generated readable projections are preferred where coverage exists; hardened comparison is limited to a genuine remainder.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A checker survives after its target is generated, or is removed while an ungenerated seam remains.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Wholesale retirement loses a proven signal; wholesale retention blocks replacement by generation.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: An unguarded residual allows structural accounts to drift.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Only shared structural claims are compared; human narrative remains locally authored.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Conformance tooling begins policing non-structural prose.

coding_notes: Conditional axes remain off-vertex and off bias. The rejection of wholesale retirement is historical; the final #274 mechanism remains unresolved.

title: Resolve the schema-to-Rust binding seam
decision_statement: Epic 256 has not yet chosen whether to generate and gate Rust bindings and validators from the self-hosted model inside this epic or narrow the epic's closure claim and retain schema-to-Rust conformance as an explicit sequenced follow-on.

sources.excerpt: The owner states PR #778 did not generate the full Rust struct/validator layer and requires the epic to choose inclusion with a regenerate gate or an explicitly narrowed claim and follow-on.
The open issue distinguishes schema-file mirror fidelity from the unguarded schema-to-Rust struct and validator semantics seam.

alternatives: Include generated Rust bindings and validators in epic 256 and close with regenerate-and-diff.
Close epic 256 at schema/prose generation and name #777 as a sequenced follow-on.
accepted_cost: No scope, schedule, or residual-conformance cost has yet been accepted.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Including the seam protects end-to-end semantic fidelity; deferral enables a nearer honest milestone.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Either outcome must state its boundary explicitly and must not imply the seam is closed.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A schema-level success claim obscures divergent runtime semantics.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Generation would replace hand-maintained bindings; deferral preserves the current implementation path temporarily.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The follow-on option retains the gap as named work rather than declaring it solved.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A bootstrap boundary persists without sequencing or ownership.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A generated binding gate enforces cross-language coherence; deferral leaves Rust implementation autonomy within an explicit boundary.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Parity scope must be truthful under either outcome.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Implementation autonomy becomes silent contract divergence, or shared conformance overreaches the epic's feasible scope.

coding_notes: Explicitly off bias counts. High confidence refers to the existence and shape of the unresolved fork, not to either direction.
